benefits.title: Benefits advice
benefits.question: What would you like help with?

routes.title: Check what I could get
steps: Use the Turn2us calculator for an estimate. It does not decide a claim or assess whether you qualify for PIP.
Already getting benefits? Ask an adviser before starting Universal Credit: a new claim can end some existing benefits.

routes.title: Claim Universal Credit
steps: Create or sign in to your Universal Credit account on the government website. Submit the claim to start it.
No bank account, email or access to a phone? You can ask at a Jobcentre. If you cannot apply online, the government guide gives the phone route.

routes.title: Start or finish a PIP claim
steps: Starting a claim? The postcode checker tells you whether you can apply fully online. GOV.UK also explains how to start by phone or post.
Already started online? Sign in to your PIP account. If DWP sent a personal link or paper form asking how your disability affects you, use that instead. Citizens Advice has help for each question.

links.label: Check if I can start PIP online
Sign in to an existing online PIP claim
GOV.UK: all ways to claim PIP
Citizens Advice: help with each PIP question

routes.title: Speak to a benefits adviser
steps: For a new Universal Credit claim, contact Help to Claim by phone or chat.
For PIP, another benefit or advice about switching, use Find an Adviser to find a service near you.

routes.title: No fixed address: ask a charity about HSBC
steps: If you are experiencing homelessness or housing difficulties, ask your support charity whether it is part of Shelter’s Breaking the Cycle programme.
A caseworker from a participating organisation arranges the HSBC appointment. Agree where your card, PIN and letters can safely be sent. An ordinary branch visit does not start this scheme.

links.label: HSBC: how the no fixed address service works
Shelter: get help to open an account

routes.title: No fixed address or standard ID: ask Barclays
steps: Barclays lists its Basic Current Account as an option if you have no fixed address. Use its account page to arrange a branch or Barclays Local appointment.
Before travelling, explain which documents you have and ask what alternatives the bank will accept. The bank makes the decision.

links.label: Barclays: Basic Current Account and appointments

routes.title: Temporary address: compare other accounts
steps: If you are in a hostel or temporary accommodation, ask the bank if it accepts an occupancy agreement or a letter from the manager. If you are in a refuge, ask staff before sharing any address.
Lloyds: start a current account application. You cannot apply for its Basic Account directly; Lloyds may offer it after its checks. Ask about a branch appointment if applying online is difficult.

Nationwide: check the FlexBasic eligibility and documents on its account page, then follow its application options. Ask about acceptable proof before applying. These are ordinary accounts, with no guarantee that a particular address or document will be accepted.

links.label: Shelter: ways to prove a temporary address

identification.title: Get ID
identification.question: What do you need the document for?

routes.title: Everyday photo ID or proof of age
steps: Ask the organisation what it accepts before paying. CitizenCard is a UK photo ID and proof-of-age card. It does not prove a right to work or replace a passport for international travel.
Apply with a photo and choose a verification route. If you have no accepted photo ID or eVisa, check whether a professional can confirm your details from records or verify a document.

links.label: CitizenCard: apply and check the fee
CitizenCard: check who can be a referee

routes.title: Get a provisional driving licence
steps: Use DVLA’s guide to check the age, eyesight and permission-to-live requirements first.
Check the fee and accepted identity documents, then choose the online or postal route. A licence is not proof of a right to work.

routes.title: Replace a birth certificate or get a passport
steps: For a birth registered in England or Wales, order an official copy through the General Register Office. The guide links to other registration services. A birth certificate is not photo ID.
For a first adult British passport, check who can apply and which documents you need before paying.

links.label: Order a copy of a birth certificate
Apply for a first adult British passport

legal-advice.title: Free legal advice
legal-advice.question: What kind of legal help do you need?

routes.title: Find a free legal advice clinic
steps: Use LawWorks to search by town or postcode and area of law. Read the clinic’s entry for its opening times, topics and booking instructions.
A first advice appointment does not automatically include someone representing you in court. Tell the clinic about any deadline when you contact it.

links.label: LawWorks: find a free legal advice clinic
Law Centres Network: get local help

routes.title: Check if legal aid could pay
steps: Use the government checker to see if your issue and circumstances may qualify. Follow its advice about finding a legal adviser.
For civil legal aid, an adviser applies for you. If you have court papers or a deadline, contact an adviser promptly.

routes.title: Ask about a volunteer barrister
steps: Advocate considers applications in England and Wales for help from a volunteer barrister. Read its criteria and gather the case papers it asks for.
It usually needs at least three weeks after receiving the complete application. Help is not guaranteed. If a deadline is close, do not wait for Advocate before seeking other legal help.

links.label: Advocate: check the process and apply

routes.title: I’m applying for jobs
steps: Start with one job advert. Match your skills and experience to what it asks for; volunteering, caring or learning can give you examples.
Use the National Careers Service guide to make or update your CV. Only share documents with the employer through a trusted route.

links.label: National Careers Service: build a CV

routes.title: I need to prove my right to work
steps: British or Irish citizen? Check the passport and document options. For example, a UK birth certificate can be used with an official document showing your name and National Insurance number.
For other nationalities, GOV.UK explains when a share code or eligible immigration documents can be used. An ordinary photo ID card alone is not enough.

routes.title: I’m starting a job or need support
steps: Give your employer your P45 if you have one. If you do not, use HMRC’s starter checklist so payroll can work out your tax code.
You can start work before receiving a National Insurance number if you can prove your right to work. If a health condition or disability affects work, check Access to Work for possible support.

links.label: Check or apply for a National Insurance number

courses.title: Find a course
courses.question: How would you like to learn?

routes.title: Try free learning at home
steps: OpenLearn from The Open University has free short courses. “Succeed in the workplace” helps you explore your skills and plan a next step.
You can browse the free course materials before deciding whether to study further. OpenLearn short courses are different from enrolling on a degree.

routes.title: Explore a funded qualification
steps: Learning Curve Group offers flexible online courses. Choose a subject and check the entry and funding rules for that course.
Free study depends on eligibility. Before enrolling, ask about costs, time each week and what happens if you need to stop.

routes.title: Find a course near me
steps: Search the National Careers Service by town or postcode. Try a skill such as “digital skills”, “English” or “customer service”.
Choose online or classroom learning, then check dates, fees, accessibility and how to enrol with the course provider.

links.label: National Careers Service: find a course
